description: Initial calibration cases for duplicate-relation evidence. Each two-Memory case calibrates one relation and does not prescribe all-pairs enumeration. EXACT and SURFACE_EQUIVALENT are deterministic relations; the remaining labels preserve semantic equivalence, partial overlap, insufficient scope, and distinct meaning.

cases.scenario: Two directly owned Memories store the same bytes.

memories.content: The main entrance closes at 5 p.m.
The main entrance closes at 5 p.m.

cases.scenario: Formatting differs, but conservative comparison normalization preserves the same words and punctuation.

memories.content: The main entrance closes at 5 p.m.
The  main entrance closes at 5 p.m.

expected.rationale: Outer trimming and horizontal-whitespace normalization yield the same comparison key without changing stored content.

cases.scenario: The wording differs while audience, place, time, modality, and operational state remain the same.

memories.content: During construction, the main entrance closes at 5 p.m.
The main entrance is open only until 5 p.m. during construction.

expected.rationale: Each Memory can replace the other without losing a condition, exception, audience, or operational consequence.

cases.scenario: One Memory contains the same closure fact plus a unique causal claim.

memories.content: The underground parking garage is closed during construction.
The underground parking garage is closed during construction because waterproofing work is underway.

expected.rationale: The closure fact overlaps, but replacing the second Memory with the first would lose the stated cause.

cases.scenario: The Context contains a main entrance and a separate staff entrance, but one Memory does not identify which entrance it means.

memories.content: Staff may use the entrance after 5 p.m.
Staff may use the staff entrance after 5 p.m.

expected.rationale: The pair is equivalent if the unspecified entrance denotes the staff entrance and distinct otherwise; the available scope does not decide.

cases.scenario: The Memories concern one parking facility but make independently revisable claims about different access modes.

memories.content: Vehicles cannot enter the parking garage during construction.
The parking garage pedestrian door remains open to staff during construction.

expected.rationale: Vehicle entry and staff pedestrian access are different operational predicates, so neither Memory can substitute for the other.
